title: Build a tiny counter
summary: A page can keep a number in JavaScript and show it in an element.

blocks.text: A page can keep a number in JavaScript and show it in an element. Each click updates the number and then updates the displayed words.
The HTML examples are complete small page parts. Use this site's HTML Run button. Put the script after the elements it uses so those elements already exist.

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `textContent` reads or replaces plain text inside an element. It does not interpret the supplied words as HTML.
`addEventListener` waits for the named event before calling the function you pass to it.
`querySelector` finds the first matching element. Check for a missing result when the element is optional.

blocks.text: Three clicks make the output show 3. Reloading this example starts again at zero.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: This example keeps the count only in memory. It does not save a record after a reload.
